case_comparison: The reports overlap in time, but their observed states differ. A had an optical loss isolated to one ONT on a branch whose other 15 monitored ONTs remained up. B remained optically normal and registered while its user-network-interface link was down. C had no recorded ONT or Ethernet state transition and is on a separate OLT and feeder. No common alarm or shared topology is present in the bundle.
case_bundle_text: Incident bundle, 3 September, 17:45–18:30. Case A: ONT C-051 is on OLT-6 PON port 1/3. At 17:58 it reported loss of signal and its session dropped. The monitoring record shows that 15 other ONTs on the same PON port remained registered and in service. C-051 returned to service at 18:21; the bundle records no shared-port alarm or field repair. Case B: ONT C-208 is on OLT-6 PON port 1/7, a different branch. At 18:02 its subscriber reported no connectivity. The ONT remained registered with normal optical status, while its Ethernet user-network interface showed link down from 18:01 to 18:19. Case C: ONT C-330 is on OLT-9 and a separate feeder. Its subscriber reported slow application response from 18:04 to 18:11, but the ONT remained registered and the recorded optical and Ethernet states did not change. No PON-port or upstream alarm was recorded for the incident window. Question: Do the reports indicate one shared outage, or are localized incidents more likely? Identify what the available evidence can and cannot establish.
scope_assessment: The available evidence favors separate localized incidents over a shared PON or upstream outage. Case A is an isolated optical loss on one ONT, Case B has a link-down indication limited to its user-network interface, and Case C has a service complaint without a corresponding recorded access-state change. The cause of C remains undetermined.
inference_rationale: Temporal overlap by itself does not establish a common outage. The distinct topologies and non-matching failure states weigh against a single shared PON or upstream event. A's loss of signal was not accompanied by failures among the other monitored ONTs on that port; B's recorded change was at its user-network interface; and C has only a reported performance symptom with no corroborating access-state change. The evidence supports a localized-or-unresolved interpretation, but does not identify the underlying cause of any individual case.
shared_outage_indicators: No common PON branch or upstream component is identified across the cases: A and B use different PON ports, and C is on a different OLT and feeder. There is no recorded shared-port or upstream alarm, and the three cases do not share the same access-layer status change.
single_subscriber_indicators: Only C-051 reported loss of signal on its branch while 15 other ONTs on that PON port remained in service. C-208 had a user-network-interface link-down interval while its optical and registration states remained normal. C-330's complaint was limited to application response, with no recorded change in ONT registration, optical status, or Ethernet state. These are distinct, subscriber-specific observations rather than a common access failure signature.

case_comparison: A and B are topologically separate at the PON level but converge on U-2. Their sessions dropped together while their optical and registration states remained normal, and both recovered as the U-2 forwarding alarm cleared. C had a later power-loss event on a separate OLT and uplink; its service returned with premises power restoration, not with the U-2 alarm clearing.
case_bundle_text: Incident bundle, 22 June, 10:20–11:10. Case A: ONT B-201 is on OLT-2 PON port 2/1 and splitter cabinet S-8. Case B: ONT B-244 is on OLT-2 PON port 2/2 and splitter cabinet S-11. These are separate PON branches, but the topology record shows that both PON ports use aggregation uplink U-2. At 10:32 both subscribers lost their service sessions. Both ONTs remained registered, reported normal optical status, and showed no loss-of-signal event. The OLT event log recorded a forwarding alarm on U-2 from 10:32 to 10:47; both sessions recovered when the alarm cleared. Case C: ONT B-309 is on OLT-4, PON port 1/5, and a different aggregation uplink. At 10:35 it lost power; its service returned at 11:05 after power was restored at the premises. No other ONTs on its branch were reported down. Question: Is this one common PON outage, a shared upstream event plus an isolated fault, or a set of unrelated subscriber faults?
scope_assessment: The cases indicate a mixture: A and B are consistent with a shared upstream service-path issue on aggregation uplink U-2, while C is consistent with an isolated premises power fault.
inference_rationale: The shared timing alone would be suggestive, but the common uplink and matching forwarding-alarm interval provide more specific support for a shared upstream issue affecting A and B. Their normal optical states make a shared optical break on either individual PON branch less consistent with the recorded evidence. C has a separate timeline, topology, and explicit local power event, so combining it with the U-2 incident would overstate the outage scope. The bundle supports the distinction without establishing a deeper cause for the uplink alarm.
shared_outage_indicators: A and B lost service at the same time despite being on separate PON branches. Both remained registered with normal optical status, and the recorded forwarding alarm on their common aggregation uplink began and cleared at the same times as the service disruption and recovery. The separate branch on OLT-4 is not part of that shared topology.
single_subscriber_indicators: Case C has a distinct, locally reported power loss at the premises and recovered when power was restored. It is on a different OLT and aggregation uplink, and no other ONTs on its branch were reported down. Those observations fit an isolated subscriber-side event rather than the U-2 service disruption.

scope_assessment: The evidence strongly favors a shared fault affecting the PON branch through splitter cabinet C-17, rather than three independent subscriber faults.
case_comparison: A, B, and C share the same access branch and show nearly simultaneous loss of signal and session drops, followed by recovery immediately after the common connector was serviced. The comparison ONT has a different PON port and splitter cabinet and did not show a service change. The timing and topology therefore align the affected cases with one another, not with all ONTs on OLT-3.
case_bundle_text: Incident bundle, 14 May, 14:00–14:30. Case A: ONT A-104 is on OLT-3, PON port 1/8, through splitter cabinet C-17 and distribution leg D-4. At 14:06 it reported loss of signal and its service session dropped. Case B: ONT A-117 uses the same PON port, splitter cabinet, and distribution leg; it reported loss of signal at 14:07 and its session dropped. Case C: ONT A-123 is on that same shared branch; it reported loss of signal at 14:08 and its session dropped. A comparison ONT on OLT-3 PON port 1/9, served by a different splitter cabinet, remained registered and in service throughout. At 14:17 a field team cleaned and reseated the common feeder connector at C-17. The three affected ONTs regained optical service between 14:18 and 14:19, and their sessions recovered. Question: Do the observations point more strongly to a shared access fault or to separate subscriber faults? Which evidence is most useful for judging scope?
inference_rationale: Coincident optical loss among multiple ONTs sharing the same branch is stronger evidence of a common access fault than of coincidental premises faults. Their near-simultaneous recovery after work at a shared feeder connector further supports that interpretation. The unaffected ONT does not contradict a branch-scoped fault because the bundle places it on a separate PON port and splitter cabinet. The evidence supports the scope conclusion, though it does not establish the physical condition of the connector beyond the recorded work and recovery.
shared_outage_indicators: Three ONTs on the same PON port, splitter cabinet, and distribution leg reported loss of signal within two minutes and lost service. They recovered within two minutes of work on the common feeder connector. The ONT on a different PON port and splitter cabinet stayed in service during the event.
single_subscriber_indicators: The bundle provides no distinct premises-level trigger for any of the three affected ONTs. Their closely spaced optical failures and recovery after work on a shared feeder are inconsistent with a pattern of unrelated, isolated subscriber faults. The unaffected ONT is a useful topology comparison, but it is on a different branch.
